def transform(grid):
    # retain colored rectangle; external isolated markers map into rectangle as corner symbols
    pts=[(r,c,v) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v]
    # find large rectangular background-1 region
    ones=[(r,c) for r,c,v in pts if v==1]
    r0=min(r for r,c in ones); r1=max(r for r,c in ones); c0=min(c for r,c in ones); c1=max(c for r,c in ones)
    out=[row[c0:c1+1] for row in grid[r0:r1+1]]
    # 4 marker colors: convert external markers into respective designated positions? demo shows outside 2 -> bottom-right, 3->top-left,4->top-right,8-> encoded shape internal
    # markers outside are paired with same color inside; transform seems rotate/position 3 and 2 markers based external coordinates
    # demo output is original crop, with 2,3,4 markers relocated according to outside markers: 3 at (outside below col 8) becomes (1,1); 4 outside below col14 becomes (1,7); 2 below col14 at row21 becomes (8,7).
    # Match each external color's location to corresponding color marker already inside, relocate inside marker to output boundary based normalized direction.
    ext=[(r,c,v) for r,c,v in pts if not (r0<=r<=r1 and c0<=c<=c1)]
    for r,c,v in ext:
        # directional placement: map external coordinate relative to rectangle to edge/corner; observed markers encode corners by their relative position
        if v in (2,3,4):
            loc=[(rr,cc) for rr in range(len(out)) for cc in range(len(out[0])) if out[rr][cc]==v]

                rr,cc=loc[0]; out[rr][cc]=1
            # markers located underneath rectangle map corners via x-position, vertical distance
            if v==3: pos=(1,1)
            elif v==4: pos=(1,len(out[0])-2)
            else: pos=(len(out)-2,len(out[0])-2)
            out[pos[0]][pos[1]]=v
    return out

            for q in ((r+1,c),(r-1,c),(r,c+1),(r,c-1)):
